correctness.rationale: D and Phi count two separate classes of nonempty subsets of [n], as made explicit by the proof and verifier; Phi is not conditioned on membership in D. Each deficit includes the empty subset. All multiples-of-r subsets fail the D condition because r does not divide n, and every failing gcd is at least r. For Phi the corresponding assertions follow from p being the least prime divisor of n. Counting subsets supported on multiples and taking a union bound traps each deficit between 2^floor(n/d) and (n+1) times that lower bound, with d=r or p. This also works at n=2 with r=3 and an empty upper-bound sum. Taking logarithms and accounting for both floors gives the asserted (looser) uniform error; r≥3,p=2 on even n and r=2,p≥3 on odd n give both inequalities for the unscaled ratio. The fibers r=k are the difference of the multiples of L_(k−1) and L_k; a new LCM valuation occurs exactly at a prime power. The least-prime fibers follow from finite inclusion–exclusion. The even tail is bounded by 1/L_K and the tail avoiding all primes through Q by the finite Euler product, which tends to zero by comparison of its reciprocal with the harmonic sum. This justifies taking the infinite limit for bounded continuous h, using uniform continuity on the eventual compact range. Each parity contributes total mass 1/2.
residual_risks: The exact arithmetic checks through n=1500, direct subset enumeration through n=16 and finite arithmetic fiber checks through 200000 are corroboration; the proof, not these checks, establishes the limiting law.
